question: If robots can do many tasks but cost more than people, how should we plan for work?
reflection: When we measure carefully what machines can and cannot do yet, we gain time to prepare people for the changes ahead.

Google is sending AI chips into orbit

one_line: Open AI models are proving strong at finding security holes, while new research suggests robots are capable but still too costly to replace most physical work.

top_stories.title: Robots are capable but rarely cheaper than people
top_stories.what: Anthropic estimates robots can do about three quarters of physical job tasks, yet they are cheaper than human workers for only a tiny share of work today.
top_stories.why: Cost, not capability, may set the pace of automation, which changes how workforce studies should model job risk.

top_stories.title: Open models win a hacking contest
top_stories.what: A security firm reportedly won an authorised bug-hunting contest using teams of agents built on open-weight models from a Chinese lab, finding flaws in live systems.
top_stories.why: Organisations holding personal data need to assume attackers now have cheap AI help, and test their own systems more often.

top_stories.title: China sets rules for AI companions
top_stories.what: New Chinese rules require AI companion services to say clearly they are not human, protect minors and avoid encouraging emotional dependence.
top_stories.why: These rules give a ready list of behavioural safeguards that other regulators and product teams can test and adapt.

saudi_lens.text: China's companion rules offer a reference point for Saudi regulators considering how to protect young users of AI chat apps.
Slow robot cost declines suggest Saudi automation plans in logistics and construction may still rely on human workers for years.

idea.title: Task automation cost study
idea.pitch: Score common physical jobs by what robots can do and what it would cost, to give a realistic timeline of automation risk.
idea.first_step: Pick ten common job titles and list their main tasks from an occupational database.

idea_kids.title: Robot or helper card game
idea_kids.pitch: Children sort cards showing everyday jobs into what a robot could do, what a person does best, and what needs both.
idea_kids.first_step: Draw twenty simple job cards, such as cooking, cleaning, teaching and fixing a bike.

When a person comes to rely on a system, such as a chatbot, for comfort in a way that crowds out human support.

concepts.summary: Robots can technically do many tasks, but cost keeps most physical work in human hands for now.
AI agents find software flaws faster, helping both defenders and attackers.
People forming emotional bonds with chatbots, now drawing specific regulation.
